title: Deuteronomy Bible Quiz - Chapter 15
description: Ten questions on Deuteronomy 15: the year of release, generosity to the poor, freeing Hebrew servants and the firstborn animals.

questions.text: What were they to do at the end of every seven years?
questions.explanation: At the end of every seven years they were to cancel debts.

answers.text: Cancel debts
Count the people
Rebuild the altar
Move the camp

questions.text: From whom may payment still be required when Yahweh's release has been proclaimed?
questions.explanation: A creditor must not require payment from his neighbor and his brother, but of a foreigner he may require it.

answers.text: A brother
A neighbor
A foreigner
No one at all

questions.text: What does Deuteronomy 15:6 promise about lending and borrowing?
questions.explanation: Yahweh will bless them: they will lend to many nations but will not borrow, and rule over many nations.

answers.text: They will borrow from many nations
They will lend to many nations but not borrow
They will neither lend nor borrow
They will lend only to Egypt

questions.text: How should they treat a poor brother within their gates?
questions.explanation: They must not harden their heart or shut their hand, but surely open their hand and lend him enough for his need.

answers.text: Send him away to another city
Help him only in the seventh year
Make him their servant
Open their hand and lend him enough

questions.text: Which wicked thought does Deuteronomy 15:9 warn against?
questions.explanation: They must beware of thinking, "The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand," and then giving the poor brother nothing.

answers.text: "The harvest will surely fail this year"
"He is not from my own tribe"
"The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand"
"My father never helped his father"

questions.text: What does Deuteronomy 15:11 say about the poor?
questions.explanation: The poor will never cease out of the land; therefore they are commanded to open their hand to the needy and poor.

answers.text: They will all become rich
They will leave the land
They will be cared for only by the Levites
They will never cease out of the land

questions.text: In which year must a Hebrew servant be let go free?
questions.explanation: A Hebrew man or woman sold to them serves six years, and in the seventh year they must let him go free.

answers.text: The seventh year
The third year
The tenth year
The fiftieth year

questions.text: What must the master do when he lets a Hebrew servant go free?
questions.explanation: He must not let him go empty, but furnish him liberally out of his flock, threshing floor and wine press.

answers.text: Send him away with nothing in his hand
Give him freely from flock, threshing floor and wine press
Make him pay the price of his freedom
Give him a field and a house of his own

questions.text: What is done if the servant says, "I will not go out from you," because he loves the house?
questions.explanation: The master takes an awl and thrusts it through his ear to the door, and he becomes his servant forever.

answers.text: His hair is cut off
His hand is marked with a sign
He is given a new name
An awl is thrust through his ear

questions.text: What must they not do with a firstborn animal that is lame or blind?
questions.explanation: If it has any defect, such as being lame or blind, they shall not sacrifice it to Yahweh, but eat it within their gates.

answers.text: Eat it within their gates
Sacrifice it to Yahweh
Let the unclean and the clean eat of it
Eat it like the gazelle and the deer
